title: Field Orientation
objectives: Explain why ecologists use quadrats to sample a habitat
Lay out a quadrat and identify every organism inside it
Record counts accurately for later analysis

steps.title: Meet the ranger

sequence.instruction: Talk to Ranger Okafor outside the field station.
sequence.hint: Follow the yellow arrow and the compass at the top of the screen.
npcLines: Welcome to the reserve! I'm Ranger Okafor. We think the disturbed lot next door is losing plant diversity, and we need data to prove it.
We measure biodiversity with quadrats: square frames we lay on the ground. We count every organism inside, then compare habitats.
Grab a quadrat kit from the table by the station, and I'll show you on the practice plot.
how: Follow the yellow arrow and the compass at the top of the screen.
Walk with W A S D or the arrow keys. On an iPad, drag the joystick in the bottom-left corner.
When you are close, a button appears at the bottom of the screen. Press E or tap the button.
Read each line, then press Continue.

intro: Welcome to the field station! In this short mission you will learn how ecologists measure biodiversity in the field.
Scientists can't count every plant in a whole habitat. Instead they count small sample areas and use them to estimate the whole habitat.
vocab: The variety of living things in an area.
The place where an organism lives and finds what it needs.
A small part you study to learn about the whole.
A square frame laid on the ground to mark a sample area. Ours is 2 m × 2 m.

steps.title: Gear up

sequence.instruction: Pick up a quadrat kit from the table by the field station.
sequence.hint: It's the white frame and clipboard on the wooden table.

feedback.correct: Quadrat kit collected: a 2 m × 2 m frame, a field guide and a tally sheet.

how: Walk to the wooden table beside the field station (follow the yellow arrow).
When you are close, a button appears at the bottom of the screen. Press E or tap 'Pick up'.

steps.intro: Every team uses the same equipment so results from different places can be compared fairly.
vocab: Pictures and descriptions that help you identify each species.
A running count of each species you find.

steps.title: Practice plot

sequence.instruction: Walk to the practice plot (marked P) and lay out your quadrat.
sequence.hint: Stand next to the orange flag marked Plot P and press E (or tap the button).

feedback.correct: Quadrat placed. Only count what's inside the frame.

how: Follow the compass to the practice plot near the station to the orange flag marked P.
Press E or tap 'Lay quadrat' to put down your frame.

sequence.instruction: Count every organism in the practice quadrat. Choose a species from the field guide, then tap each one you see.
sequence.hint: Compare shapes and colors with the field guide swatches. Every plant must be tallied before the plot is complete.

feedback.correct: Practice plot recorded. Nice careful counting!

how: A photo of the quadrat opens. Only organisms inside the frame are in the photo.
On the right, choose a species from the field guide list and read its description.
Tap every organism of that species in the photo. A green check marks each one you counted.
Choose the next species and repeat until every organism has a check. The plot saves itself when you finish.
A wrong tap shows a red circle and costs a few points, so compare shapes and colors with the guide first.

intro: Now practice. A quadrat count is only useful if it is careful: count only what is inside the frame, and count each organism exactly once.
vocab: One kind of organism, like a daisy or a fern.
The counts exactly as you recorded them, before any math.

sequence.instruction: Tell Ranger Okafor what you found on the practice plot.
npcLines: Great work! See how every species in the frame now has a count? That's your raw data.
Next, run the full Habitat Biodiversity Survey: two quadrats each in the meadow, the forest and the disturbed lot. Then we'll see which habitat is most diverse.
how: Walk back to Ranger Okafor (follow the yellow arrow).
Press E or tap the button to talk.
